subject: Post-call: Integration & Function Catalog / Next Steps
body:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@edgenova.io>, Priya Sarker <priya.sarker@edgenova.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Integration & Function Catalog / Next Steps

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the productive demo earlier. Quick recap + my recommended next steps so we can get a minimal integration proof-of-concept (POC) running next week.

Key takeaways from today's discovery:
- Goal: embed Redwood inference into EdgeNova's content ingestion pipeline to provide structured summarization, & a reranker for search results.
- Priority features: structured output (JSON schema), tool/function calling for enrichment (web fetch + analytics), and embeddings + reranker to boost relevance.
- Constraints: SSO + software token rotation via your KeyVault; on-prem routing for EU customers later in Q4.

Proposed immediate deliverables (POC scope):
1) SDK setup + auth: quickstart using Redwood Node SDK with service token + optional mTLS for Private. We can provide a short snippet and config.
2) Function catalog: small set of tool definitions we recommend for POC (search-index lookup, external fetch, analytics enrich).
3) Structured output: enforce schema via Redwood's structured output feature and a post-parse reranker circuit.
4) Error & fallback patterns: recommended retries, parallel fallback to smaller model variant, and safe-mode responses when external tools time out.

Concrete next steps / owners:
- EdgeNova: share a short sample of the search index API (Swagger or brief curl). Priya — can you drop the Swagger link? (Open item)
- Redwood (Marcus): provide 1-page function catalog + example SDK snippet for parallel tool calls by EOD tomorrow.
- Redwood (Camila): schedule a 45-min technical handoff with your infra/security and our solutions engineering — proposed slots Thu/Fri.

Auth notes (high level):
- For hosted POC: service token (short-lived) + role scoping. We'll walk through token rotation patterns using your KeyVault (we support issuing tokens via our private control plane if you want short-lived credentials).
- For Private/on-prem: mutual TLS + KMS/HSM integration is available; Marcus can sketch the network diagram.

Function catalog (POC minimal):
- name: search_lookup
  description: query internal search index by query text; returns top-K candidate docs with ids and snippets
  inputs: {"query": "string", "k": "int"}
  output: {"candidates": [{"id":"string","score":"float","snippet":"string"}]}

- name: fetch_document
  description: fetch full document by id from customer store (used to enrich the candidate with metadata and sections)
  inputs: {"doc_id":"string"}
  output: {"content":"string","metadata":{"source":"string","published":"string"}}

- name: analytics_enrich
  description: attach engagement signals (clicks, recency, category) to candidates for reranker features
  inputs: {"candidates": "list", "user_ctx": "object"}
  output: {"augmented_candidates": "list"}

Function orchestration guidance (recommendations):
- Tool choice: prefer coarse-grained tools that do one thing well (search_lookup, fetch_document). Keep network-bound calls isolated and idempotent.
- Parallel tools: run search_lookup and analytics_enrich in parallel after initial candidate fetch to minimize tail latency; then run fetch_document for top 3 serially or in a small concurrent pool (N=3).
- Error handling: adopt a 2-level fallback:
  1) soft-fail: if non-critical enrichment (analytics_enrich) times out (>=500ms), continue with candidates sans enrichment and mark reranker input as degraded.
  2) hard-fail: if search_lookup fails, fallback to a degraded model-only retrieval (embedding-based nearest-neighbor with smaller model) and return a confidence flag.
- Timeouts & retries: short network timeouts (200-500ms) with exponential backoff, max 2 retries for idempotent calls. For non-idempotent operations, avoid automatic retries and surface to operator.

Example SDK patterns (pseudo):
- parallel = await redwood.call(["search_lookup", "analytics_enrich"], inputs)
- if (parallel.search_failed) -> fallback to embeddings-based retrieval
- for top in parallel.candidates[:3]: await redwood.call("fetch_document", {doc_id: top.id})

Structured output & reranker flow:
- Use structured output schema to have model return candidate ids + explanation tokens. Post-process with analytics_enrich outputs, then run a small learned reranker (server-side) using combined features (model score, recency, analytics signals).

Deliverables Marcus will supply:
- One-page function catalog (JSON list) with recommended timeouts and retry semantics
- Node/Go SDK snippet for parallel calls + a sample error-policy config
- A minimal YAML for structured output schema for our summarizer

Attachments: edge-nova-mapping-v1.xlsx (sample mapping you shared) and our RFI answers PDF.

--
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0119

Thanks Camila — this looks great. Quick clarifications from our side:
- For the embeddings fallback, what model sizes are you recommending for the embedding index vs. the main reranker?
- Can the SDK do native retries + per-tool timeout config, or do we need to implement orchestration in our app layer?

Also: Priya will post the Swagger export for the search API by end of day. If possible, can Marcus add the sample mTLS config for Private? We're evaluating both hosted and private POCs.

Alex
Head of Search, EdgeNova

-----Original Message-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@edgenova.io>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 13:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Integration & Function Catalog / Next Steps

Alex / Priya — quick answers inline.

- Embeddings vs reranker model sizes: start with a compact embedding model (e.g., 2B-ish) for dense-index retrieval, and use a mid-sized reranker (6-13B) tuned for pairwise scoring for the POC. We'll provide recommendations tied to expected latency budget.

- SDK capabilities: Redwood SDK supports per-tool timeout and retry policies natively (you can set tool-level config during registration). For more advanced orchestration (conditional branching, complex fan-in), you may choose to orchestrate in-app or use our server-side routing + function-chain feature. We'll include both patterns in the snippet.

- mTLS sample: attaching a short mTLS sample config and network diagram in the follow-up (will drop to the Drive link Marcus shared).

I'll assemble the one-pager and SDK snippet and post by 5pm PT. Camila — I'll sync with you on the handoff invite.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
